name: Poonjar Palace
tagline: A 600‑year‑old royal house at the foot of the Western Ghats
summary: Poonjar Palace is a timber-and-stone royal complex in Meenachil taluk that preserves the Poonjar dynasty's antiques, temple replica and monthly rituals—ideal for palace tours and winter festival…
description: Poonjar Palace is the historic seat of the Poonjar royal family in Meenachil taluk, Kottayam. The complex mixes Kerala timber architecture with Pandya/Chera influences and houses a compact museum of royal objects.

The palace matters for historians and visitors because it preserves rare objects — a single‑piece wooden droni (ayurvedic couch), palanquins, chandeliers, palm‑leaf manuscripts and carved stone lamps — plus a striking replica of the Madurai Meenakshi shrine on the grounds.

Visitors get a close, low‑crowd palace experience: guided or self‑guided viewing of the galleries, short rituals (the palace still observes monthly poojas) and easy day‑trip access from Kottayam, Pala and Erattupetta.

Poonjar also serves as a staging point for nearby high‑range trails and hill destinations (Vagamon, Ilaveezha Poonchira), and local festivals and community events cluster here during the winter tourist season.
highlights: Museum of royal objects: palanquin, wooden droni, chandeliers and palm‑leaf documents.
Replica of Madurai Meenakshi shrine within the palace complex.
Rare rock‑cut chuttuvilakku (row of lamps) at the nearby Sastha temple.
Monthly palace rituals still observed by the royal household.
Easy day‑trip from Kottayam, Pala and Vagamon — good base for hill trails.
Local cultural events and village festivals stage in the area during the winter season.

sections.heading: Background
body: The Poonjar royal line traces its origin to a Pandya branch that settled in central Travancore centuries ago; the palace complex reflects that long history and local temple traditions. The present palace and museum preserve objects used by the family and by the court over several centuries.

Kerala tourism and district heritage materials describe the palace as roughly 600 years old and highlight its mixed architectural influences and the presence of a Madurai Meenakshi temple replica on site.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Walk the palace galleries to see the collection: bronze lamps, a carved single‑piece droni used in traditional medicine, palm‑leaf manuscripts, weapons, jewel boxes and an old palanquin. The museum atmosphere is intimate — expect a short, focused visit.

Visit the small temple replica and the Sastha temple nearby to view the carved chuttuvilakku (stone row of lamps) and experience the local ritual calendar; the palace continues to host monthly thevarapuja/Manthily rituals and annual temple festivals.

Combine the palace visit with short drives to Vagamon or Ilaveezha Poonchira for hill walks, or time your visit to coincide with local cultural events staged by the panchayat during the winter season.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Poonjar Palace lies on the Pala–Erattupetta route and is reachable by road from Kottayam (about 40–45 km). The nearest major railhead is Kottayam station; the nearest major airport is Cochin International (COK). Confirm opening times and any guided‑tour arrangements before you travel.

Winter (November to February) offers the most pleasant weather and the greatest chance of local festivals and community events. Facilities are basic — plan a daytime visit and combine it with nearby heritage or hill attractions for a full day.

latest.text: Poonjar Grama Panchayat lists Keralotsavam events in the Poonjar area on Oct 31 and Nov 7–8, 2026 — local cultural programming that can be paired with palace visits during the winter season.
Coverage of the Mangaladevi temple festival at Poonjar recorded the continuing palace rituals and the monthly Manthily/Pathmamittu ritual, underscoring the living ceremonial calendar at the site.

visitorInfo.bestTime: November to February (cool weather and many local events)
visitorInfo.howToReach: By road (Pala–Erattupetta route) from Kottayam ~40–45 km; nearest rail Kottayam station (~42–43 km); nearest airport Cochin International (~74–86 km). Confirm local connections and bus timings before travel.
etiquette: Confirm palace opening times and whether a guide or prior permission is required — official sites list the palace but not fixed daily schedules.
Wear modest clothing when visiting the palace temple and neighboring shrines and remove footwear where required.
Combine the palace visit with Vagamon or Ilaveezha Poonchira for hill walks; hire a local driver or guide for easier access to nearby village festivals.
If you want to see monthly rituals or festival-day displays of special objects (some items come out only on ritual days), check dates with the panchayat or on‑site staff in advance.
